# PAL16L8 - Programmable array logic, 10 inputs, 8 active-low three-state outputs (6 with feedback)

Package DIP-20 · family PAL · catalogue file [catalog/chips/PAL16L8.json](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/RetroSchematic/blob/master/src/catalog/chips/PAL16L8.json)

## Functions

| Output pin | What it does |
|---|---|
| 12,13,14,15,16,17,18,19 | Programmable AND array feeding fixed OR gates, 7 product terms per output plus one product term that enables that output; all outputs active low. What each output computes is set by the fuses blown when the chip was programmed. |

| From | To | Edge | Typ ns | Max ns | Conditions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| any input or feedback | any output | PLH | 25 | 35 | commercial range (VCC 4.75-5.25 V, TA 0-75 C), test load R1 200 ohm, R2 390 ohm (1983 handbook page 3-10); the datasheet gives one tPD for both output edges |
| any input or feedback | any output | PHL | 25 | 35 | commercial range (VCC 4.75-5.25 V, TA 0-75 C), test load R1 200 ohm, R2 390 ohm (1983 handbook page 3-10); the datasheet gives one tPD for both output edges |
| any input | any output | PZX | 25 | 35 | commercial range (VCC 4.75-5.25 V, TA 0-75 C), test load R1 200 ohm, R2 390 ohm (1983 handbook page 3-10); tPZX, input to output enable through the enable product term |
| any input | any output | PXZ | 25 | 35 | commercial range (VCC 4.75-5.25 V, TA 0-75 C), test load R1 200 ohm, R2 390 ohm (1983 handbook page 3-10); tPXZ, input to output disable through the enable product term |

## Not known

- Load capacitance of the switching test is not on the pages read.
- Minimum delays: the datasheet gives none.
- The fuse map of the card's chip (not read).
- The speed grade of the chips on the card: the reading says PAL16L8 with no letter, so the standard grade is used here (the A grade is 25 ns max).

## Notes

How to read this chip: put it in a device programmer that supports the type and read the fuse map (only possible if the security fuse was not blown; the 1983 handbook, printed page 3-20, describes the security fuses). Save it as a JEDEC file, turn the fuse map into equations with a disassembler, and write those equations into a per-card file for this board position. Never put equations in this catalogue file: it describes the blank device. Pin names here are made up from the pin function shown on the MMI logic diagram (I = dedicated input, IO = output that also feeds back into the array, O = output with no feedback) plus the pin number, because the datasheet numbers the pins but gives them no names. The 8 rows of each output group on the logic diagram are 1 enable term and 7 OR terms (1983 handbook page 3-33). Card 3207 uses this type at 9E, 21E, 24B, 21A and 13C.

## Sources

- [Monolithic Memories PAL Handbook, 3rd edition, 1983](https://bitsavers.mirrorservice.org/components/mmi/_dataBooks/1983_MMI_PAL_Handbook_3ed.pdf) - printed 3-3, 3-4 (PDF 29-30: family table, DIP pinout), 3-10 (PDF 36: operating conditions, electrical and switching tables), 3-33 (PDF 59: logic diagram), 6-356 (PDF 496: an example PAL16L8 drawn with GND on pin 10 and VCC on pin 20); PAL16L8 (standard speed)
- [Monolithic Memories PAL/PLE Handbook, 5th edition, 1986](https://bitsavers.mirrorservice.org/components/mmi/_dataBooks/1986_MMI_PAL_PLE_Handbook_5ed.pdf) - printed 2-19, 2-20 (PDF 42-43: Medium 20 series: 10 dedicated inputs, 8 outputs of which 6 I/O, outputs enabled by a product term, all active low; DIP and PLCC pinouts); PAL16L8
